- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable HTML5/Three.js 3D isometric action roguelike inspired by Hades and dark-fantasy anime JRPGs.

## Requirements
- Include a gothic 3D dungeon, dynamic lighting, smooth movement, melee/ranged combat, procedural rooms, upgrade shop, affinity/romance dialogue, and unlockable character gallery.
- Use chibi/billboard characters for gameplay and high-resolution 2D portraits/illustrations for UI.
- Heroines should be mature, glamorous, alluring, curvy anime characters with flirtatious personalities.
- Load 2D art from local PNG files in `assets/characters/`, with clean fallbacks for missing artwork.

## Decisions
- Built from a blank project using vendored Three.js.
- Used locally rendered SVG-to-PNG artwork because image-generation credentials were unavailable.
- Created procedural synthetic soundtrack/SFX instead of external audio assets.
- Included `seraphine`, `mirelle`, `ysolde`, and `vesper` character assets and data.
- Replaced portrait and gallery artwork iteratively to improve face, silhouette, and gothic styling.

## Work State
### Completed
- Initialized the project and installed Three.js.
- Vendored Three.js modules and postprocessing support.
- Created generated character PNG artwork and clean placeholder fallback support.
- Built base HTML structure, HUD, menus, dialogue, shop, gallery, controls, pause, and result UI.
- Created CSS styling for the gothic visual presentation and responsive layouts.
- Implemented data, save persistence, audio engine, and core 3D world code.
- Implemented procedural room/dungeon-related systems in `src/world.js`.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- External image-generation credentials were unavailable, so custom image generation could not be used; local bespoke artwork was substituted.

## Next Move
1. Verify the game runs in a browser and test title, gameplay, combat, shop, dialogue, gallery, and restart flows.
2. Capture and review browser screenshots, especially at desktop and mobile viewport sizes.
3. Fix any runtime/import, Three.js, UI, or generated-art issues found during verification.
4. Replace placeholder-oriented character files in `assets/characters/` with final custom PNG artwork if desired.
5. Preserve and test `localStorage` save behavior across runs.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Main game markup and application entry structure.
- `styles.css`: Gothic UI and responsive presentation.
- `src/main.js`: Main gameplay initialization and runtime orchestration.
- `src/world.js`: Three.js scene, procedural rooms, enemies, lighting, and world rendering.
- `src/data.js`: Character, enemy, shop, dialogue, and flavor data.
- `src/save.js`: Persistence and run/bond/perk tracking.
- `src/audio.js`: Procedural music and combat SFX.
- `src/art.js`: Local PNG loading and clean canvas fallback behavior.
- `assets/characters/`: Portrait, gallery, and chibi PNG artwork.
- `tools/art/common.mjs`: Shared SVG/PNG character-art helpers.
- `tools/art/portraits.mjs`: Portrait artwork renderer.
- `tools/art/gallery.mjs`: Full-body gallery artwork renderer.
- `tools/art/chibi.mjs`: Chibi billboard artwork renderer.
- `vendor/three.module.js`: Vendored Three.js module.
- `vendor/addons/`: Vendored postprocessing, shaders, and supporting modules.

## Important Context
- Character assets use replaceable filenames such as `seraphine_portrait.png`, `seraphine_gallery.png`, `mirelle_gallery.png`, `ysolde_gallery.png`, and `vesper_chibi.png`.
- Missing images route through `src/art.js` to generated canvas placeholders.
- Saves use the `localStorage` key `emberwake_save_v1`.
- The implementation relies on browser ES modules and the import map mapping `three/addons/` to `./vendor/addons/`.

# Worker Agents Skills

This repository bundles the baseline skills installed by [Worker
Agents](https://github.com/agents-dev/workerAgents).

The bundled skills are available under [`skills/`](skills/):

- `mcp-duckgo` — imported from `aahl/skills@mcp-duckgo`.
- `image-search` — imported from `z0gsh1u/oh-my-writing-skill@image-search`.
- `gauntlet-loop` — imported from `robonuggets/gauntlet-loop@gauntlet-loop`.
- `load-sketchfab-threejs` — local asset inspection, normalization, and Three.js/PlayCanvas A/B viewer skill.
- `opencode-zen-completions` — use the OpenCode Zen chat completions API for implementation work.

The original upstream licenses are preserved in
[`third-party-licenses/`](third-party-licenses/).
## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable HTML5/Three.js 3D isometric action roguelike inspired by Hades and dark-fantasy anime JRPGs.

## Requirements
- Include a gothic 3D dungeon, dynamic lighting, smooth movement, melee/ranged combat, procedural rooms, upgrade shop, affinity/romance dialogue, and unlockable character gallery.
- Use chibi/billboard characters for gameplay and high-resolution 2D portraits/illustrations for UI.
- Heroines should be mature, glamorous, alluring, curvy anime characters with flirtatious personalities.
- Load 2D art from local PNG files in `assets/characters/`, with clean fallbacks for missing artwork.

## Decisions
- Built from a blank project using vendored Three.js.
- Used locally rendered SVG-to-PNG artwork because image-generation credentials were unavailable.
- Created procedural synthetic soundtrack/SFX instead of external audio assets.
- Included `seraphine`, `mirelle`, `ysolde`, and `vesper` character assets and data.
- Replaced portrait and gallery artwork iteratively to improve face, silhouette, and gothic styling.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game structure, gothic UI, data, persistence, audio, and core 3D world systems.
- Fixed room cleanup to remove room lights while preserving the player light, reset obstacles per room, and retain full portal data.
- Added Vesper as player-avatar data outside the romance/gallery character order.
- Moved the interaction prompt outside the HUD container and raised its stacking order.
- Vendored missing `vendor/three.core.js` after browser console errors; the title screen now renders.
- Browser-tested title, hub, dialogue and reply, and gallery flows; captured screenshots under `screenshots/`.

### Active
- Continue browser verification of shop, gameplay/combat, pause, restart, and save persistence; inspect the captured shop screenshot and test desktop/mobile layouts.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `screenshots/shop.png` and finish checking the shop flow.
2. Exercise a run, combat, pause, result/restart, and `localStorage` persistence in the browser; review console errors.
3. Capture and review mobile viewport behavior and fix any issues found.
4. Check `git status` and preserve the current uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Runtime orchestration, UI interactions, and gameplay loop.
- `src/world.js`: Three.js scene, procedural rooms, enemies, lighting, and rendering.

- `screenshots/`: Browser captures including title, hub, dialogue, gallery, and shop.

- Changes are uncommitted.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable HTML5/Three.js isometric action roguelike inspired by Hades and dark-fantasy anime JRPGs.
- Deliver gothic dungeon combat and procedural progression alongside a shop, affinity dialogue, and an unlockable character gallery.

## Requirements
- Include smooth movement, melee/ranged combat, dynamic lighting, procedural rooms, upgrades, romance dialogue, and a character gallery.
- Use chibi/billboard characters in gameplay and high-resolution 2D portraits and full-body illustrations in UI.
- Heroines should be glamorous, mature-proportioned, curvy anime characters with stylish fantasy outfits and flirtatious, teasing personalities.
- Load replaceable local PNG artwork from `assets/characters/`, with clean fallbacks when artwork is missing.
- Build the game without clarification; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Built from a blank project with vendored Three.js and browser ES modules.
- Used locally rendered SVG-to-PNG artwork because image-generation credentials were unavailable.
- Created procedural synthetic soundtrack and sound effects instead of external audio assets.
- Added `seraphine`, `mirelle`, `ysolde`, and `vesper`; Vesper is a player avatar, not part of the romance/gallery character order.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game structure, gothic UI, character/game data, persistence, audio, and core 3D world systems.
- Fixed room cleanup, lighting preservation, obstacle resets, portal data, interaction prompt placement, and Vesper player-avatar handling.
- Vendored missing `vendor/three.core.js`; title screen renders.
- Browser-tested desktop title, hub, dialogue/reply, gallery, shop purchase, combat, boon selection, room progression, victory/result, and save persistence.
- Completed a simulated full run through the final boss and verified saved results; save key is `emberwake_save_v1`.
- Improved player visibility, combat survivability, enemy spacing, shop pricing, hub placement, and title-screen mobile logo sizing.
- Improved mobile hub layout and dialogue portrait framing; mobile title, hub, dialogue, and gallery were browser-checked.
- Captured screenshots under `screenshots/`.

### Active
- Review `screenshots/mobile-shop.jpg` and finish checking the mobile shop layout and interaction.
- Verify mobile gameplay controls, combat, pause, and result screens; check remaining console warnings and responsive overflow.
- Review final changes and preserve the uncommitted work.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `screenshots/mobile-shop.jpg`; fix any mobile shop layout or interaction issues.
2. Test mobile run controls and the gameplay, pause, and result flows; review browser console output.
3. Check `git status` and retain all current uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Runtime orchestration, UI interactions, and gameplay loop.
- `src/world.js`: Three.js scene, procedural rooms, enemies, lighting, and rendering.
- `src/data.js`: Character, enemy, shop, dialogue, and flavor data.
- `src/save.js`: Save persistence and run/bond/perk tracking.
- `index.html`: Main markup and browser module setup.
- `styles.css`: Gothic UI and responsive layouts; recent mobile fixes.
- `src/art.js`: Local PNG loading and missing-art fallback behavior.
- `assets/characters/`: Local PNG character artwork.
- `vendor/three.core.js`: Core module required by the vendored Three.js module.
- `screenshots/`: Desktop and mobile verification captures, including `mobile-shop.jpg`.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed the project files as untracked.
- Desktop full-run verification reached victory at depth 5; a shop purchase and persistence across reloads were verified.
- Mobile browser checks used a Chrome browser session after Chromium was unavailable; mobile shop screenshot is captured but has not yet been reviewed.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable HTML5/Three.js isometric action roguelike inspired by Hades and dark-fantasy anime JRPGs.
- Finish mobile verification and polish while preserving the existing uncommitted project work.

## Requirements
- Include smooth movement, melee/ranged combat, dynamic lighting, procedural rooms, upgrades, romance dialogue, and an unlockable character gallery.
- Use chibi/billboard characters in gameplay and high-resolution 2D portraits and full-body illustrations in the UI.
- Use replaceable local PNG artwork from `assets/characters/`, with clean fallbacks when artwork is missing.
- Build without clarification; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Built from a blank project with vendored Three.js and browser ES modules.
- Used locally rendered SVG-to-PNG artwork because image-generation credentials were unavailable.
- Created procedural synthetic soundtrack and sound effects instead of external audio assets.
- Added `seraphine`, `mirelle`, `ysolde`, and `vesper`; Vesper is a player avatar, not part of the romance/gallery character order.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game structure, gothic UI, character/game data, persistence, audio, and core 3D world systems.
- Fixed room cleanup, lighting preservation, obstacle resets, portal data, interaction prompt placement, and Vesper player-avatar handling.
- Vendored missing `vendor/three.core.js`; title screen renders.
- Browser-tested desktop title, hub, dialogue/reply, gallery, shop purchase, combat, boon selection, room progression, victory/result, and save persistence.
- Completed a simulated full run through the final boss and verified saved results; save key is `emberwake_save_v1`.
- Improved player visibility, combat survivability, enemy spacing, shop pricing, hub placement, and title-screen mobile logo sizing.
- Improved mobile hub layout and dialogue portrait framing; mobile title, hub, dialogue, and gallery were browser-checked.
